files.evidence-naming.txt:
EVIDENCE for position naming-confusion (wrong IDs cause most "broken" reports):

1. NIM API expects: moonshotai/kimi-k3 (all lowercase).
2. HuggingFace repo is: moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (capital K, capital K3). Anyone copying the HF ID to NIM gets a 404.
3. Our own herd used a local alias 'kimi-k3-nim' that was NEVER a real model ID on any surface — on 2026-09-17 an agent repointed it at dead nvidia nemotron models while keeping the kimi name, because it misdiagnosed a 401 (bad key) as a routing failure.
4. Kimi Code API uses yet another ID: 'k3' via https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1.
5. vLLM requires the 'kimi_k3' tool parser — using 'kimi_k2' "mis-parses K3 and the chat content comes back empty" (third-party serving guide). A parser mismatch looks exactly like "model broken" (empty responses).
6. Pattern observed twice: credential/endpoint/config failures get misdiagnosed as model failures — by our own agent (09-17) and by internet users (404 on wrong ID → "model broken").

spec:
# Question: Is Kimi K3 actually broken on NVIDIA NIM, and what is the correct way to call it?

Background: Kimi K3 (moonshotai, 2.8T MoE) has a model card on build.nvidia.com and weights on HuggingFace. Online reports say it is 'broken on NIM'. Our own herd kimi-k3 route (via Pollinations/OpenRouter, never via NIM directly) died on 2026-09-20 with 401s/402s. Three positions compete: (1) NIM is fine, failures are transient infra; (2) NIM's hosted endpoint is genuinely unreliable, use HF providers instead; (3) the reputation is mostly wrong model IDs per surface.

Judge which position best fits the evidence, with a synthesis of what to actually do.
